cases.sentence: Эй, все, кто жаждет, придите к ___, и те, у кого нет денег, приходите, получайте еду и ешьте.
cases.translation: Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters; and you who have no money, come, buy and eat.
cases.explain: The preposition к (to) governs the dative case when indicating movement toward something.

cases.sentence: Приходите, получайте вино и молоко без денег, бесплатно. Зачем тратить деньги на то, что не ___?
cases.translation: Come, buy wine and milk without money and without price. Why do you spend money for that which is not bread?
cases.explain: Хлеб is the subject of the implied predicate in the rhetorical question, taking the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Слушайте меня внимательно и ешьте хорошее. Пусть душа ваша порадуется сытной ___.
cases.translation: Listen diligently to me, and eat that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in abundance.
cases.explain: The verb порадуется (will rejoice) with the preposition in takes the instrumental case for that which brings joy.

cases.sentence: Внимайте и приходите ко мне. Слушайте, чтобы жива была ___ ваша.
cases.translation: Turn your ear, and come to me. Hear, and your soul will live.
cases.explain: Душа is the subject of the verb была (was/would be), requiring the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Я заключу с вами вечный ___, нетленную милость, обещанную Давиду.
cases.translation: I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David.
cases.explain: The verb заключу (I will make) takes the accusative case for its direct object завет (covenant).

cases.sentence: Как дождь и снег не сходят с небес и не возвращаются, не напоив ___, но делают ее способной рождать и произращать.
cases.translation: For as the rain comes down and the snow from the sky, and doesn't return there, but waters the earth, and makes it grow and bud.
cases.explain: The verb напоив (watering) takes the accusative case for its direct object землю (earth).

cases.sentence: Так и слово мое, что исходит из моих уст. Оно не вернется ко мне напрасным, но совершит то, чего я хочу. И достигнет того, для чего я его ___.
cases.translation: So is my word that goes out of my mouth: it will not return to me void, but it will accomplish that which I please, and it will prosper in the thing for which I sent it.
cases.explain: The verb послал (sent) is in the past tense and agrees with the singular masculine noun слово.

cases.sentence: Вы выйдете в радости, проводят вас с миром. Горы и холмы запоют перед вами ___, а все деревья в поле будут рукоплескать.
cases.translation: You shall go out with joy, and be led out with peace. The mountains and the hills will break out before you into singing; and all the trees of the fields will clap their hands.
cases.explain: The verb запоют (will sing) takes the accusative case for its direct object песни (songs).

reading.ru: Эй, все, кто жаждет, придите к водам, и те, у кого нет денег, приходите, получайте еду и ешьте.
reading.question: Who is being invited, and what are they invited to do?
options: Everyone who is thirsty is invited to come to the waters and eat without money
Only the rich are invited to a feast
People with money should buy expensive food
Those who are hungry should steal bread
reading.correct: Everyone who is thirsty is invited to come to the waters and eat without money
reading.explain: The text says 'Hey! Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat!'

reading.ru: Зачем тратить деньги на то, что не хлеб? Свои трудовые на то, что не насыщает.
reading.question: What question is being asked about spending money and labor?
options: Why waste money and effort on things that are not truly satisfying?
How can we save more money for ourselves?
What is the best way to earn money?
Should we always spend all our earnings?
reading.correct: Why waste money and effort on things that are not truly satisfying?
reading.explain: The passage asks 'Why do you spend money for that which is not bread, and your labor for that which doesn't satisfy?'

reading.ru: Я заключу с вами вечный завет, нетленную милость, обещанную Давиду.
reading.question: What does God promise to make with his people?
options: An everlasting covenant and sure mercies promised to David
A temporary agreement that will expire
A contract that must be renewed each year
A law that will be broken
reading.correct: An everlasting covenant and sure mercies promised to David
reading.explain: The verse states 'I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David.'

reading.ru: Как небо выше земли, так мои пути выше ваших путей, и мои мысли выше ваших мыслей.
reading.question: What does this verse teach about the difference between God's ways and human ways?
options: God's ways are as much higher than human ways as heaven is higher than earth
God's ways are exactly the same as human ways
Human ways are higher than God's ways
There is no difference between them
reading.correct: God's ways are as much higher than human ways as heaven is higher than earth
reading.explain: The verse makes this comparison: 'As the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways.'

reading.ru: Как дождь и снег не сходят с небес и не возвращаются, не напоив землю, но делают ее способной рождать и произращать.
reading.question: What does rain and snow do when they come from heaven?
options: They water the earth and make it able to grow and produce
They stay in the clouds and never reach the ground
They damage the crops and hurt the plants
reading.correct: They water the earth and make it able to grow and produce
reading.explain: The verse says 'the rain comes down and the snow from the sky... waters the earth, and makes it grow and bud.'

reading.ru: Вы выйдете в радости, проводят вас с миром.
reading.question: How will the people depart, and what will accompany them?
options: They will go out with joy and be led out with peace
They will be forced to flee
reading.correct: They will go out with joy and be led out with peace
reading.explain: The text says 'You shall go out with joy, and be led out with peace.'
